name: The Emperor of Palamecia // The Lord Master of Hell
oracle_text:
{T}: Add {U} or {R}. Spend this mana only to cast a noncreature spell.
Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, if at least four mana was spent to cast it, put a +1/+1 counter on The Emperor of Palamecia. Then if it has three or more +1/+1 counters on it, transform it.
blocked_sentences: {T}: Add {U} or {R}. Spend this mana only to cast a noncreature spell.

needs.what: a negated entry in a `mana_restriction` group -- a way to write "spend this mana only to cast a NONcreature spell", i.e. a restriction that is satisfied when a named type or subtype is ABSENT from the spell's characteristics. Concretely: let a group entry be `{"not": "creature"}` (loader `_restriction_name` in src/automtg/cards/loader/mana.py, which today accepts only a literal name or `{"chosen_type_of": "self"}`), carry the negated names alongside the required ones on `ManaRestriction`'s groups, and have `ManaSource.permits` (src/automtg/engine/mana.py) require `required <= purpose.names` AND `not (forbidden & purpose.names)` instead of the bare subset test it does now.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `mana_restriction` ships and is the right home for this line, but it is purely positive: `_restriction_groups` compiles each group to a `frozenset` of lowercased literal type/subtype names, and `ManaSource.permits` answers with `any(group <= purpose.names ...)` against `costs.spell_purpose`, whose `names` is just the flat lowercased set of the spell's types and subtypes. Nothing in that chain can express absence. The two spellings available both misprint the card. (a) `"noncreature"` as a literal loads -- the loader's shape check only asks that an entry look like a word -- and then matches nothing ever, because no spell has a type or subtype called "noncreature"; the mana would be permanently unspendable, which the loader's own comment calls out as the safe-but-silent failure. (b) Enumerating the noncreature types as an any-of, `["artifact", "enchantment", "instant", "sorcery", "planeswalker", "battle"]`, over-permits every artifact creature and enchantment creature spell, because `permits` sees "artifact" in the purpose's names and never learns that "creature" is also there -- a strictly better card than the one printed. Trigger filters already have the negation (`not_types` is honoured in `matches_card_filter`) and selectors have `not_types`/`not_subtypes`; the restriction language is the one place it is missing, and it is the same one-word idea.
needs.note: The rest of the card is expressible today and needs nothing new. The second line is a `spell_cast` trigger with `filter: {"not_types": ["Creature"]}` and `controller: "you"`, an intervening-if `{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"mana_spent_of": {"binding": "subject"}}, "right": {"const": 4}}` (the trigger's `subject` binding is the cast spell, and `costs.pay_mana` writes `obj.mana_spent` before the spell_cast event fires), then `add_counters` followed by an `if` on `{"counters_on": {"counter": "+1/+1", "objects": {"self_only": true}}} >= 3` wrapping `{"op": "transform", "objects": {"self_only": true}, "to_back": true}`. The back face, The Lord Master of Hell, is an ordinary `back_face` entry with an `attacks` trigger dealing `damage` to each opponent for `{"count": {"zone": "graveyard", "controller": "you", "not_types": ["Creature", "Land"]}}`. Land this one negation and the whole card can be authored unchanged.
